instructions: Slice the 8 oz mushrooms. Chop the onion, peel and dice the 2 carrots and dice 2 ribs of the celery. Mince the 2 garlic cloves.

Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium high. Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them alone for 6 to 7 minutes, until the undersides are well browned. Stir and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more, then move them to a bowl.

Turn the heat down to medium and add the 1 tbsp butter. Add the onion, carrots, celery and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and see-through.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Put the mushrooms back in, sprinkle over the 2 tbsp flour and stir for 1 minute, until you can't see any dry flour.

Pour in the 4 cups broth a little at a time, stirring and scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Add the 3/4 cup wild rice, 1 bouillon cube, 1/2 tsp thyme and 1/2 tsp pepper and bring it to a boil.
Cover the pot, turn the heat down to low and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is tender and some of the grains have split open.
Meanwhile, pull 2 cups of meat off the rotisserie chicken and chop it into bite-size pieces. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.
Stir the chicken, 3/4 cup corn and 1/2 cup cream into the soup. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, uncovered. Keep it at a low bubble. A hard boil can split the cream.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the parsley. Taste it, and add up to the remaining 1/4 tsp salt if it's flat.
Serve it hot. For lunches, let the rest cool and keep it in containers in the fridge for up to 4 days. The rice thickens it as it sits, so reheat each portion gently with a splash of water.
method_notes: All three build the soup on onion, carrot and celery, thicken it with a little flour and finish with cream or half-and-half and parsley. Spend With Pennies browns the mushrooms first, cooks the wild rice blend right in the broth with thyme and a bouillon cube, and adds cooked chicken, corn and cream for the last 10 to 15 minutes. Rotinrice cooks plain wild rice separately and uses half-and-half and a larger pot, and Craving Home Cooked browns raw chicken in the pot and stirs in a separate cream roux. This follows Spend With Pennies, whose pot it calls 6 servings, written here as 4 lunch bowls with meat from a rotisserie chicken.
